assertion_results.text: Commands are documented with explicit invocation syntax and expected outcome per command
assertion_results.evidence: Each command has a code invocation and description: `deploykit init` with "create or validate the deployment configuration"; `deploykit plan` with "preview the changes that will be applied"; `deploykit apply` with "execute the deployment plan"; `deploykit rollback` with "revert the latest deployment".

assertion_results.text: Preconditions or ordering constraints are stated explicitly (e.g. must run init before apply)
assertion_results.evidence: The output states "Most workflows follow this order: 1. `init` — prepare deployment configuration 2. `plan` — preview the changes that will be applied 3. `apply` — execute the deployment 4. `rollback` — revert a previous deployment" and "Only run `apply` after reviewing the output from `plan`."

assertion_results.text: Writing avoids ambiguous pronouns/vague references that would confuse an automated reader
assertion_results.evidence: The output uses explicit command names in constraints such as "Run `plan` before applying changes" and "Do not skip `init` when working in a fresh checkout or newly created environment"; references to commands are named rather than relying on unclear pronouns.
